newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela ship draught limit may hit oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela ship draught limit may hit oil exports.

text.p: A 36-foot draught restriction for oil tankers using Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo shipping channel could cut crude oil exports by up to 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) for the duration of the restriction, shipping sources in Venezuela said on Thursday.

The Maracaibo harbour master imposed the 36-foot restriction, down from a normal 39.6 foot draught, on Monday night after the Greek-flagged Olympic Sponsor ran aground near the ocean entrance to the channel. The Olympic Sponsor was carrying 477,000 barrels of medium density crude and had a draught of 39 foot, shipping sources said.
The tanker was "safely aground" just outside the channel marker buoys on Thursday afternoon and a rescue team was planning to attempt to float it on Friday.
The Maracaibo harbour master said the 36-foot restriction would be lifted only when the Olympic Sponsor had been refloated.

A shipbroker said a typical tanker with a 39 foot draught would be able to carry 84,000 tonnes of crude and a 36 foot restriction would cut this to 75,000 tonnes. A fall of 9,000 tonnes equates to approximately 55,000 barrels of medium/heavy crude.
On average, about three half-million barrel tankers leave Lake Maracaibo per day.

Some of the shortfall could be made up by more chartering more ships to use the channel, but this was only a partial solution because most of the loading jetties in the Lake were already working at full capacity, a shipping source said. Also, tankers have to be fixed weeks in advance.
